note.text: Ethiopian forces defeated an invading Italian army at Adwa in {1896}, under Menelik II's leadership with important roles for Ethiopian commanders and Empress Taytu. Disputes over Italian claims and the Wuchale treaty formed part of the background. Mobilisation, arms, leadership and local knowledge contributed to the outcome. The victory preserved independence against that invasion and became a wider symbol of resistance. It does not mean Ethiopia was never later invaded: the Italian assault in the twentieth century was a separate episode.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A historical explanation should connect more than one factor rather than crediting victory to a single heroic name. A painting of Adwa can show later memory and symbolism, but its arrangement of figures is not necessarily a precise battlefield plan. The Smithsonian's object description explicitly distinguishes historical significance from artistic arrangement.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Arrange background, mobilisation, battle and consequences. Distinguish military outcome from a claim of timeless immunity from invasion. When using art as evidence, ask when it was made and what it commemorates; do not read every detail as a contemporary eyewitness record.
